items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: He played with Brubeck later, didn’t he?

ctx.x: like, well you made $2.50 an hour as a musician. And when you were making $6.00 a night and all you could eat and drink, that was good money. So basically that’s when I decided I really wanted to be a musician. And even though the money wasn’t an awful lot, you know, there wasn’t a requirement, the cost of living was down, so you didn’t have to pay a lot of money. You could rent a house for like $20 a month, stuff like that. And it was very cheap. Of course you didn’t make a lot of money but it didn’t cost a lot…
He played with Brubeck later, didn’t he?

Yeah. Senator Eugene Wright. I was in high school and he called me to work with his band. In fact I worked with his band until I went to the service. So like there were a lot of different reasons why I wanted to play music.
